attacks.vector: masked-regression on e2e seed guard (chrome-reachability.spec.ts test 4)
attacks.evidence: Read the full test-4 body and setLayoutMode() in packages/app/e2e/agentic-terminal/chrome-reachability.spec.ts. The sessionStorage guard (`if (sessionStorage.getItem("__setLayoutModeSeeded")) return`) is set on the FIRST document load (goto("/")) and is already SET by the time the toggle-triggered reload occurs, so the init script early-returns on that reload and does NOT re-seed -- it neither writes nor overwrites anything on the document the test actually evaluates. The post-reload assertion (`expect(await page.evaluate(() => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("settings.v3") ?? "{}").general?.newLayoutDesigns)).toBe(true)`) reads real, unmasked, product-persisted localStorage state via page.evaluate against the live reloaded document -- not a test-controlled value. Traced 3 concrete regression scenarios: (1) product fails to persist the toggle (localStorage write broken) -> post-reload value stays false -> `.toBe(true)` fails explicitly (readable failure, not a silent pass); (2) click/onChange never fires at all -> no reload ever occurs -> `await reloadSettled` (registered before the click) hangs to timeout (explicit failure); (3) localStorage says true but the render never reacts (a store-reactivity regression) -> the assertion PASSES but the immediately following `page.waitForSelector('[data-slot="titlebar-v2"]')` times out (explicit failure). No path found where a genuine product persistence/reload regression produces a silent green. The guard's only effect is preventing the TEST's OWN init script from re-clobbering the just-persisted value -- it does not suppress or paper over product-side failures.

attacks.vector: coverage-genuineness (does app.test.tsx's suite protect against the isolated-registry trap being reintroduced in app.tsx?)
attacks.evidence: app.test.tsx DOES mount a genuine, non-stub CommandProvider (imported from @/context/command, confirmed real via command.tsx:248). HOWEVER: neither `SharedProviders` (app.tsx:286, not exported) nor `AppInterface` (app.tsx:545, exported but never imported by any test file -- confirmed via `grep -rln SharedProviders|AppInterface packages/app` = only app.tsx, index.ts, entry.tsx, all production wiring, zero test files) is ever rendered by app.test.tsx. The suite instead imports only the bare `AgenticCommands` function and mounts it into an ENTIRELY TEST-CONSTRUCTED tree (buildTree()/TestLeaves(), app.test.tsx:201-230, 180-188) that always wires AgenticCommands and the sibling CommandProbe under ONE shared CommandProvider the test itself builds. This tree is structurally independent of app.tsx's actual JSX composition. Consequence: if a future change reintroduces the FORBIDDEN site-(iii) trap directly inside app.tsx's SharedProviders/AppInterface (e.g., wraps `<AgenticCommands/>` in its own `<CommandProvider>` back at/near the old :582 site), app.test.tsx's 6 tests would keep passing UNCHANGED -- none of them re-import or re-render app.tsx's real composition, so none can observe the regression. The evidence file's own adversarial_review_note (9.json line 38) claims this was 'Substantiated: ... the sibling-probe invariant was validated by simulating the forbidden site-(iii) fix directly' -- I grepped .architect-team/diagnostic-research/agentic-commands-context/counter-evidence-20260719T163707Z.md and the whole diagnostic-research tree for 'site-(iii)', 'isolated', 'simulat' and found ZERO hits; no artifact anywhere on disk documents this simulation having been performed against production code. The only unit-level negative test (app.test.tsx:353-363, 'throws ... when mounted outside CommandProvider') exercises a DIFFERENT regression mode (zero providers -> crash), not the isolated-provider silent-kill mode the trap actually is -- it does not substitute for it. Mitigating factor (why this doesn't collapse the whole story, but does not rescue the specific claim): the E2E suite (packages/app/e2e/agentic-terminal/chrome-reachability.spec.ts), which DOES exercise real app.tsx composition against a live browser, provides an actual fence -- test 1 drives the real command palette, which reads options from the SharedProviders instance via dialog owner-capture (command-palette.ts / dialog.tsx runWithOwner); an isolated-registry regression would make 'agentic.open' invisible to the palette, timing out test 1's `agenticCommand.waitFor({state:'visible'})`, and a raw no-provider regression would reproduce the original RED baseline (4/4 'Page crashed', reviews/7.json). Confirmed this e2e spec is wired into CI (.github/workflows/test.yml 'e2e' job runs `bun --cwd packages/app test:e2e:local` = `playwright test`; packages/app/playwright.config.ts testDir is './e2e' with no ignore for agentic-terminal, so chrome-reachability.spec.ts runs on every CI e2e job). So the crash class IS fenced end-to-end, but ONLY at the slow, live-browser E2E level -- NOT at the fast unit level the review's own note implies, and the specific 'simulating the forbidden site-(iii) fix' claim about the unit suite is unsubstantiated and, on direct inspection, false as literally written.

Ran from packages/app (SHELL unset per toolchain quirk): (1) `npm exec --yes --package=bun@1.3.14 -- bun test --preload ./happydom.ts ./src` -> 658 pass / 18 skip / 0 fail, 676 tests across 100 files -- exact match to 9.json tests_note's default-conditions claim. (2) `... --conditions=browser --preload ./happydom.ts ./src/app.test.tsx` -> 6 pass / 0 fail -- exact match to the claimed app.test.tsx-alone count. (3) `... --conditions=browser --isolate --preload ./happydom.ts ./src` -> 675 pass / 1 fail (src/context/server-session.test.ts, 'does not scan cached messages for user roots during history prepend') -- exact match to the claimed full-suite-with-isolate count and the named pre-existing/unrelated failure. Note: running the full suite under --conditions=browser WITHOUT --isolate produced 657 pass / 19 fail (cross-file happy-dom/computedStyle state leakage in pages/agentic-terminal/__tests__/panels-*.test.tsx) -- this is consistent with bun test's documented isolation behavior and is NOT a discrepancy against the claim, since the claim's own invocation explicitly included --isolate; re-running with the exact claimed flag reproduced the exact claimed numbers.

notes: 3 of 4 attacks held. Attack 3 (coverage-genuineness) broke: app.test.tsx's component-mount suite is real (genuine CommandProvider, genuine AgenticCommands import) but structurally cannot detect a regression where the isolated-registry trap is reintroduced inside app.tsx's own SharedProviders/AppInterface composition, because that composition is never imported or rendered by any test file -- the suite substitutes its own hand-built tree. The review evidence's claim that this was 'empirically validated by simulating the forbidden site-(iii) fix directly' has no supporting artifact anywhere in .architect-team/diagnostic-research or elsewhere on disk. The actual fence against this regression class lives one layer up, in the live-browser e2e suite (chrome-reachability.spec.ts test 1, via the real command palette), which IS wired into CI (.github/workflows/test.yml e2e job) -- so the crash/trap class is not permanently un-fenced, but the fence is at the slow E2E layer, not the fast unit layer the review implies, and the specific unit-test claim is overstated. Recommend: either add a genuine app.tsx-composition-level regression test (import and render AppInterface/a minimally-exported SharedProviders and assert palette-visible registration), or correct the review's language to stop claiming unit-level discriminating power against the site-(iii) trap that the committed test does not actually possess. Attacks 1, 2, and 4 held on direct inspection and independent re-execution: no new CommandProvider/double-registration was introduced (attack 1); the e2e seed guard cannot mask a genuine product persistence/render regression in test 4 (attack 2); and the claimed unit-test counts (658/18/0/676 default; 6/0 app.test.tsx browser; 675/1 full-suite browser --isolate, context/server-session.test.ts pre-existing) were independently reproduced exactly.
